mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in workplace mobility, as observed in the latest week, indicates a return to office-based work, which directly translates to increased foot traffic in retail and recreation areas during weekdays, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the average of the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES mobility continuing its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in parks mobility, falling below baseline, signifies a shift away from outdoor leisure activities, which will divert discretionary spending and time towards indoor retail and recreation options, causing RETAIL_REC to increase over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 0% change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days, even if PARKS mobility remains below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous increase in both transit station and workplace mobility suggests a coordinated return to pre-pandemic commuting patterns, which will synergistically boost retail and recreation activity in urban centers, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the average of the last 28 days, despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES showing continued recovery.

mechanism_narrative: When residential mobility remains elevated while grocery and pharmacy visits stabilize near baseline, it indicates a shift towards local, neighborhood-based retail and recreation, which will prevent a significant decline in overall RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls significantly below the average of the last 28 days, even with stable RESIDENTIAL and GROCERY_PHARM patterns.

mechanism_narrative: Following a significant dip in retail and recreation mobility below a certain threshold, a natural mean-reversion effect will occur as consumers seek out these activities, causing RETAIL_REC to rebound over the next one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline or remains flat in the next 7 days after falling below -30%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained high level of residential mobility indicates that a significant portion of the population continues to spend more time at home, which limits their engagement with external retail and recreation activities, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the average of the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in parks mobility combined with already low retail and recreation mobility suggests that adverse weather or seasonal factors are impacting outdoor activities, but also not yet driving people indoors to retail, leading to a continued suppression of RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 0% and RETAIL_REC is below -25%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days, despite PARKS mobility remaining low and RETAIL_REC starting from a suppressed level.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in transit station mobility, even from a low base, indicates a loosening of public transport restrictions or increased confidence in public transit, which will facilitate greater access to retail and recreation venues, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by more than 4 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days, despite TRANSIT mobility showing a significant week-on-week increase.
